subject: Post-demo: model fit recommendations + request for prompt/edge-case samples
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jane Park <jane@clevertax.com>, Alex Cho <alex.cho@clevertax.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-08T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: model fit recommendations + request for prompt/edge-case samples

Hi Jane / Alex —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs we heard:
- High-accuracy tax Q&A for small business owners (free-form questions, multi-step reasoning)
- Document ingestion for 1099s and invoices (structured extraction + entity normalization)
- Low tolerance for hallucinations on calculated totals and legal disclaimers
- Must strip sensitive PII before any telemetry leaves their VPC (redaction + audit log requirement)

Initial model fit recommendations (based on workload and latency expectations):
- For free-form Q&A: recommend a 14B instruction-tuned open model (quantized) as primary for cost/throughput, with a 70B variant as fallback for complex reasoning where accuracy matters.
- For document extraction: use a specialized smaller encoder-decoder model tuned for structured extraction (fine-tune on labeled receipts).
- Safety: enable conservative temperature and deterministic sampling for numbers, plus post-processing checks for numeric consistency.

Benchmarks and artifacts I’m linking for reference: https://drive.google.com/clevertax/eval-benchmarks (contains latency and EM/accuracy simulated on your sample dataset).

What we need from CleverTax to build a small evaluation:
1) A set of 100–200 representative prompts/questions (real customer examples if possible). CSV or simple rows are fine. Mark any prompts that are high-risk / must-not-hallucinate.
2) 50–100 document examples (anonymized PDFs) or structured extracts so we can validate extraction templates.
3) Edge-case list: 10–20 examples where current system fails today (e.g., ambiguous totals, negative refunds, multi-currency lines).
4) Redaction guidance: a short list of field types that must be stripped vs. allowed to be tokenized for model training/eval (e.g., SSN -> remove, Tax ID suffix -> allow hashed).

Suggested next steps / timeline:
- Jane: share sample prompts + one redaction policy draft by EOD Tue (2027-08-10).
- Redwood (Dylan + Marissa): spin up a lightweight eval using the 14B model on the supplied prompts and return metrics + sample outputs in 3 business days.
- Quick check-in call after that (15–20 min) to review failures and decide whether to run a 70B baseline.

Attachments we referenced in-demo are: redwood_eval_playbook.pdf (internal), and I’ve included the benchmark link above.

If it helps, we can provide a CSV template — I’ve attached a quick prompt-sample template to this thread.

Thanks —
Dylan

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
PD: (Attachment: prompt_sample_template.csv)

On Mon, Aug 8, 2027 at 2:12 PM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum:
> 
> What we need from CleverTax to build a small evaluation:
> 1) A set of 100–200 representative prompts/questions (real customer examples if possible).

Thanks Dylan — this is great and aligns with internal priorities.

We can share an initial batch. A couple of clarifications before we export: 
- For the prompts you want "real" examples — we have a mix: (a) customer support transcripts, (b) tax prep UI free-text questions, (c) programmatic agent queries. Is it OK to mix these, or do you prefer to see them separated?
- Redaction: our security team requires that SSNs and full bank account numbers are redacted at source. We can provide a mapping file that indicates redactions. Is hashed placeholders acceptable?

We’ll attach two files in the next email: clevertax_sample_prompts.csv (about 120 rows) and clevertax_edgecases.xlsx (a short list of edge-case examples). Also attaching a short note from our security lead on required redaction fields.

Couple more asks from our side:
- Can you include a column in the eval results that flags hallucination risk and numeric inconsistency?
- If the 14B model fails on a subset, how disruptive is switching to the 70B for the evaluation run (time/cost estimate)?

Appreciate it — we’ll send the files now.

—Jane
Jane Park
Head of Product | CleverTax Inc
(Attachment: clevertax_security_redaction_note.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Park <jane@clevertax.com>, Alex Cho <alex.cho@clevertax.com>
Date: 2027-08-08T16:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit recommendations + request for prompt/edge-case samples

Thanks Dylan / Jane — looping in Ben from Solutions to scope the extraction baseline. A couple notes from our side: 

- On mixed prompt types: we can accept a mixed batch but please mark the "source_type" column (support vs UI vs agent) so we can segment evals. If you can’t, we’ll sample-stratify on our side.
- Redaction placeholders: hashed placeholders are fine (please include the mapping table in a separate CSV so the audit trail is preserved).
- Output flags: we will add a hallucination risk column and a numeric-consistency check (we run a simple rule: sum of line items == reported total; flag if mismatch). We’ll provide a metrics CSV with those columns.
- Cost/time to run 70B baseline: approximate compute delta is ~4–6x the 14B run depending on sequence lengths; we’ll provide a cost estimate after we ingest the prompts. For planning, assume 4x.

Ben — can you confirm we have an extraction template ready for ingestion of sample invoices (we’ll need a small mapping for line_item -> amount/date/description). Also adding a note to Security that we’ll need the redaction policy attached to the eval job so telemetry truncation is enforced.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

On Tue, Aug 8, 2027 at 4:00 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Dylan / Jane — looping in Ben from Solutions to scope the extraction baseline.

Hi all — thanks for the quick turn. Attached are the two files Dylan requested: clevertax_sample_prompts.csv (120 rows) and clevertax_edgecases.xlsx (18 examples). We also attached the redaction mapping (clevertax_redaction_map.csv).

Notes on the attached prompts:
- Column layout in the CSV: id | source_type | prompt_text | expected_answer (optional) | risk_label (low/medium/high)
- Edge-cases sheet contains examples that break our current rules (e.g., overlapping currency tokens, two different reported totals on a single invoice, handwritten cents).
- We marked 12 prompts as "high" risk — these are where we expect the model to either refuse or require a deterministic extraction.

Next steps from our side: please run the 14B baseline and share the metrics CSV + 10 sample outputs flagged as high-risk. If the 14B accuracy on the high-risk set is below 78% EM, please include a short note on the incremental cost to evaluate with the 70B.

Thanks — we look forward to the results.

Alex
Alex Cho
Integration Lead | CleverTax Inc
(Attachments: clevertax_sample_prompts.csv, clevertax_edgecases.xlsx, clevertax_redaction_map.csv)
